name: Rolled (cast) plate glass
process: Molten glass is carried from the furnace in large iron ladles, thrown onto the cast-iron bed of a rolling table and rolled into a sheet by an iron roller (James Hartley's patent rolled plate, about 1847). The sheet is thicker and stronger than blown sheet, wavy, and translucent rather than clear when one face takes the texture of the table or roller. In the mid-19th century it roofed railway stations and greenhouses. The Oxford Museum's roof is of this family: about 8,500 diamond-shaped panels of sand-cast glass, a nominal 10 mm (8-12 mm), each with its own pattern.
